scope: G6 final formal-review batch 014: six remaining records
write_status: reviewed-only; no production insert authorized until approved records are localized and one guarded migration passes full-history isolated PostgreSQL dry-run
review_method: Opened all six current images and compared what they show with the claimed canonical project.
Verified Commons creator, source, original dimensions and license metadata through the MediaWiki API.
Checked first-party architect or operator sources for the three approved identities and design responsibility.
Queried production read-only for building-name conflicts, required broad types and active functions.

excluded.reason: The record describes generic UR housing-complex regeneration, has no year or architect, and explicitly labels its Akabanedai photograph representative rather than project-specific; a canonical building must not be invented from a typology reference.

The record describes the generic Michi-no-Eki model and links MLIT's national program, while its image is the specific Roadside Station Oguni; the CASE does not establish Oguni as its canonical design subject or identify a design author.

Phaeno identity and ZHA authorship are clear, and the Commons file is CC BY-SA 3.0, but visual review shows only a blurred interior exhibit apparatus rather than the building or its defining spatial architecture.

canonical_building.name_zh: 波特兰日本庭园文化村
canonical_building.name_ja: ポートランド日本庭園カルチュラル・ビレッジ

identity_evidence: KKAA identifies the completed 2017 Oregon civic project as four buildings arranged around a courtyard plaza and credits Kengo Kuma and Associates with named collaborators.
Commons keywords identify the photographed Tsubo-Niwa as the Cultural Village Tateuchi courtyard; visual review confirms the courtyard building context.

canonical_building.name_ja: メトロポール・パラソル

identity_evidence: J.MAYER.H identifies its 2004-2011 Seville project and documents the archaeological museum, farmers market, elevated plaza, food venues and panorama terrace.
The Commons own-work photograph by Arup clearly shows the exact timber parasol structure.

canonical_building.name_ja: フェデレーション・スクエア

identity_evidence: Fed Square documents the civic-space competition, cultural and commercial program, Lab architecture studio partnership with Bates Smart, and opening on 26 October 2002.
The Flickr-origin Commons image by Alpha clearly shows the main square and complex facades.
